title: Cullen Skink
subtitle: Scottish smoked haddock and potato soup
excerpt: A thick, creamy Scottish chowder of undyed smoked haddock, potatoes, and onion. Rich, smoky, and deeply comforting, from the fishing village of Cullen on the Moray Firth.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cullen skink takes its name from the small fishing village of Cullen on the Moray Firth in northeast Scotland. 'Skink' is an old Scots word for a shin or knuckle of beef, later extended to mean any thick soup or broth. The soup uses Finnan haddie — undyed, cold-smoked haddock — which is a speciality of northeast Scotland. The haddock is poached in milk to make a flavoured stock that forms the base of the soup. The potatoes are mashed directly into the soup to thicken it, giving a texture that is chunky but bound. Use undyed smoked haddock: the bright yellow dyed version is not traditional and gives an artificial colour to the finished soup.

content.text: Use natural, undyed smoked haddock for the best flavour and a pale, cream-coloured soup. The haddock is poached in milk and the cooking milk becomes the base of the soup, so do not discard it. Mash some of the potato directly into the soup to thicken it rather than using flour: this gives a cleaner, more natural texture. Check the seasoning carefully before adding salt as the haddock is already quite salty.

Place the smoked haddock in a wide pan. Pour over the milk and add the bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 8 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Remove the fish and set aside. Strain and reserve the poaching milk, discarding the bay leaves.

Melt the butter in the same pan. Fry the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft but not coloured. Add the potatoes, reserved poaching milk, and stock. Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

Using a spoon, roughly crush about one third of the potatoes against the side of the pan to thicken the broth. Flake the smoked haddock, discarding any skin and bones, and stir into the soup. Add the cream. Heat through gently but do not boil. Season with black pepper. Add salt only if needed. Stir in the parsley and serve.
